what: Every place where the validity or availability of a ZK, privacy, FHE or proof operation depends on something other than committed State and the transaction bytes, with the operation it gates, the committed source that decides it instead (or its removal) and the plan task that owns the change. `sites` are the detector hits attributed to an entry as [path, detector, token, occurrences]; the checker fails on a hit no entry lists and on a listed hit that is gone. `attribution` says whether the entry was written from reading its code (`read`) or assigned by a path rule (`path_rule`): a path-rule entry records where a class of names occurs and which task owns that code, not a site-by-site reading. Recording a gate establishes neither its removal nor the security of the operation behind it. Limits of the scan: it reads production Rust sources of the listed crates and the listed SDK roots as text. It does not see a gate written with none of the detected names (for example a chain-identity condition that names no network in a literal and uses none of the detected identifiers), a result selected under a Cargo feature the census does not classify as a gate, a read of a node-configuration policy field through a local variable instead of a field path, or anything built by a macro. Outside the proof path, clock readings and reviewer or approval names are scanned only in Core's admission, execution, validation and publication files. Crates outside the list are not scanned. In particular, family identifier detectors count generic CryptoImplementationUnavailable/UnsupportedImplementation names only in matching family files; tx.rs, block.rs and Torii lib.rs do not match and their generic crypto transport is outside those rows. AnonymousBallotUnavailable matches the family expression itself and is counted in those files. This limitation is regression-tested and is not evidence that compiled crypto implementations are complete.

kinds.environment: A process environment variable, or a build-time environment value.
kinds.node_local_config: Node-local configuration: a value read from this node's configuration file.
kinds.cargo_feature: A Cargo feature that compiles or selects code.
kinds.digest: A binary, source, executable, build or catalog digest used as identity.
kinds.chain_identity: A chain-ID or network condition: production versus integration, testnet versus mainnet.
kinds.readiness_qualification: A readiness certificate, a qualification signer or receipt, a reviewer signature.
kinds.activation_lifecycle: An activation transaction or bit, a lifecycle availability switch, or the typed unavailable outcome of an unfinished operation.
kinds.global_manifest: A global all-protocol manifest or a zero availability pin.
kinds.wall_clock: A wall clock or a local timeout.

statuses.open: The gate exists. The owner task removes it or moves its source into committed State.
statuses.done: Removed or moved by F.4; `tests` and `removed` are the evidence the checker holds.
statuses.unsupported: The typed error of an operation that is not implemented or not secure yet. It depends on no configuration, feature or environment and stays mandatory work of the owner; removing it must not make the operation succeed.
statuses.local_resource: A typed failure of this node's own entropy, allocator, storage, accelerator, host or platform. It is not a gate and not unfinished work: it fails a local prover or wallet call, and on the validation path it defers the local attempt and never rejects carried evidence. `tests` names the deferral tests where the owner has them.
statuses.not_a_gate: The detector hit is not a validity or availability gate; `note` says why.
statuses.out_of_plan: Outside the products of the ZK delivery plan; recorded for visibility, `note` says why.

env_read.what: A process environment variable or a build-time environment value is read.

config_env_alias.what: A node-configuration field can be set from a process environment variable.

dev_env_flag.what: A developer environment flag is consulted.

config_switch.what: An enable or assume-valid switch of the [zk] or [confidential] node configuration is read.

node_config_read.what: A service reads the [zk] or [confidential] section of the node configuration directly.

handshake_switch.what: The confidential capability a node advertises in the P2P handshake from its own configuration (`confidential.enabled`, `assume_valid`, `verifier_backend`) is read, carried or compared.

zk_settings_install.what: A complete ZK settings value, validity values included, is installed into a State. Production code installs local resources only (State::install_node_zk); the complete installer exists in test builds, so every production call site is a defect.

zk_settings_write.what: A field named `zk` (the ZK settings of a State or of a configuration value) is assigned, with `=` or a compound operator, named by the first field written below it. Production code may write local resource settings only; every other write is a defect.

pipeline_settings_install.what: A complete pipeline settings value, execution limits included, is installed into a State. Production code installs local resources only (State::install_node_pipeline); the complete installer exists in test builds, so every production call site is a defect.

pipeline_settings_write.what: A field named `pipeline` (the pipeline settings of a State or of a configuration value) is assigned, with `=` or a compound operator, named by the first field written below it. Production code may write local resource settings only; every other write is a defect.

settings_mut_borrow.what: A field named `zk` or `pipeline` is borrowed mutably (`&mut x.zk`, which is also how `mem::replace`, `mem::swap` and `mem::take` reach it) or overwritten with `clone_from`, named by the field. The settings fields of `State` are private, so outside the State modules such a line does not compile; inside them every site is listed.

default_validity_settings.what: Production code names the protocol-default verification gas schedule (`DEFAULT_ZK_GAS`) or builds a default ZK, gas or pipeline settings value (`Zk::default()`, `ConfidentialGas::default()`, `Pipeline::default()`). Metering, admission and fee bounds must take the schedule and limits frozen in the block or view they execute in; a default value passed to a meter, a host or a quote instead is a defect, so every site is listed.

node_policy_read.what: State, a block, a view or a service reads a field of the node-configuration policy sections whose validity values are not committed yet ([pipeline], [nexus], [gov], [crypto], [oracle], [fraud_monitoring], [content], [settlement]). A row is recorded when the path read is a field of one of the catalogs the resource contract records, named by the catalog field it reaches.

feature_cfg.what: Code is compiled or selected under a Cargo feature. Rows are required only for features the census classifies as validity or availability gates.

digest_identity.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names a source, binary, build, catalog or release digest. The class word starts a word of the identifier and the digest word ends one, so `resource_shape` and `ReleaseShare` do not match; a plain `commit_hash` or `commit_digest` is a commitment value and is not matched, and a builder function named `build_sha<bits>_<what>` (the verb `build` followed by a hash function and the thing built, such as `build_sha256_word_circuit_v1`) is not a build digest and is not matched.

chain_condition.what: An identifier names a production, integration, testnet, mainnet or pinned-chain condition.

chain_literal.what: A value is compared with, or matched against, a string literal that names a network (minamoto, taira, mainnet, testnet, devnet) in a crate that decides or verifies.

qualification.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names a qualification, a readiness record, a reviewer or an audit signoff. `fully_qualified` (a complete `name@domain` identifier, as in `parse_fully_qualified`) is a parsing term and is not matched.

activation.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names an activation or a lifecycle. Class `revocation_state` is derived from the source: the identifier is the name of a lifecycle enum whose variants are exactly `Active` and `Revoked`, or `Active`, `Superseded` and `Revoked`, the in-force state of a committed record. Class `constant_true` (any identifier detector) is a `const NAME: bool = true`.

unavailable.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names an unavailable, suspended or unsupported outcome. Class `local_resource` is a failure of this node's entropy, allocator, storage, accelerator, host or platform; class `version_check` is the rejection of an encoding version this release does not define; the other classes are either a gate or the accurate error of an unfinished operation.

unfinished_constant.what: A file on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path defines a `bool` constant set to `false` whose name says that something is available, implemented, qualified, ready, supported, wired, complete, verified or integrated: the compile-time record of an unfinished step, which the code that reads it turns into a refusal or a not-ready status.

global_manifest.what: An identifier names the Exact12 catalog, a capability or release manifest, or an availability pin.

wall_clock.what: A wall clock or an elapsed-time reading on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path.

core_wall_clock.what: A wall clock or an elapsed-time reading in Core's admission, execution, validation and publication files that are not on the proof path (the `wall_clock` detector covers those that are).

core_review_gate.what: An identifier in Core's admission, execution, validation and publication files that are not on the proof path names a reviewer, a signoff, an audit certificate or an approval.

time_budget.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names a timeout, a deadline or a millisecond budget. Class `height_deadline` is a deadline expressed as a block height or epoch, which is committed State and not a clock. Class `deadline_outcome` names the outcome of a deadline that has passed (`...DeadlineExpired`), a failure kind recorded from committed State.

sdk_availability.what: An SDK source names a qualification, a readiness record, a capability or release manifest or the Exact12 catalog (one row per file and class).

entries.gates: Every limit, window, verifier switch, relation-selecting verifying-key identity (Kaigi authorization and usage) and verification gas charge bound by compute_zk_consensus_policy_hash: Native PIPA-R and STARK proof and envelope sizes, batch, SCCP proof and verifier-work limits, proof retention, bridge-proof windows, confidential anchor age and policy-transition windows, registry caps and the confidential gas schedule.
entries.decided_by: The committed custom parameter `zk_validity_policy_v1` (type, protocol default and canonical structural and coherence validation in iroha_data_model; application to State in iroha_core::zk_validity_policy). An ordinary authorized `SetParameter` installs or changes it, in genesis or later; block construction freezes the policy of the predecessor's committed parameters, so a change governs the next block and the genesis block runs under the protocol default. Executor data-model reconciliation never writes it. A node installs local resources only (State::install_node_zk) and its configuration schema has no validity field (cfg.zk.node_schema).
entries.note: Verification gas is metered with the schedule frozen in each block's settings; no process-wide schedule exists (gas.process_wide_schedule, done). The two enable switches are committed fields that the plan author decided to delete (switch.zk.backend_enabled). Two more rows read or write the committed policy, not node configuration: state/authority_registry/zk_policy.rs `borrowed` projects `policy.pipa_r.enabled` and `policy.stark.enabled` of the ZkValidityPolicyV1 held by the current and predecessor committed parameters into the authority registry cell `state.zk`, and pipeline_gas_policy.rs assigns StateParameters.zk (the typed projection of the same original parameter MV value) the validated committed payload on SetParameter and the protocol default when the custom parameter is removed, as StateParameters.pipeline does for cfg.pipeline.settings_writes.

entries.gates: The validity-affecting keys of the `[zk]` and `[confidential]` sections of the node configuration: `[zk.stark]`, `[zk.sccp]`, the limits, curve, backend and switch of `[zk.halo2]`, the scalar `[zk]` caps, windows and key references, the `[confidential]` limits and windows and `[confidential.gas]`.
entries.decided_by: Removed from the node schema: a configuration that names one fails to load with the ordinary aggregated unknown-parameter error. The sections keep local resource settings only (verifier workers, queues and budgets, FASTPQ prover settings, `confidential.verify_timeout_ms`). The tracked Taira configuration and the built-in `sora-nexus-v1` profile no longer carry such keys.
entries.note: `confidential.enabled`, `assume_valid` and `verifier_backend` remain (cfg.confidential.node_switches).

entries.gates: The confidential policy hash a genesis header binds. Genesis generators (kagami `genesis sign` and `prepared`, the iroha_deploy localnet and private-root builders, the test network) hashed the authoring node configuration into it, while validation computes it from State.
entries.decided_by: Every generator signs the protocol-default hash (default_genesis_confidential_policy_hash): the genesis block runs under the protocol default on every validator. A chain authors other values only as the `zk_validity_policy_v1` parameter of its genesis manifest, as the tracked Taira template does. The function that hashes a settings value is crate-internal.

entries.gates: 23 `ZK_*` process environment variables that set validity-affecting [zk] fields of the node configuration (proof and envelope sizes, max_k, batch, enable switches, curve, backend, history caps, bridge-proof windows, parameter-set identifiers).
entries.decided_by: Removed: the fields have no environment alias. Their values are committed chain policy (cfg.zk.validity_policy).

entries.gates: Environment aliases of the local FASTPQ prover resources: execution mode, device selection and Metal tuning. The retired Halo2 verifier-lane aliases have no successor in the current Zk user schema.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: a local resource may only defer.
entries.note: None of these fields is bound by compute_zk_consensus_policy_hash; the test local_resources_survive_and_never_move_the_consensus_hash pins the split, and policy_of names every field of the settings value as policy or local resource.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of local resource fields in the [pipeline] and [gov] sections.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local.
entries.note: Read alias by alias. The eighteen PIPELINE_* aliases other than PIPELINE_GAS_TECH_ACCOUNT_ID set fields that `pipeline_validity_policy::policy_of` marks as local resources (access-set cache, caches, tracing, GPU bucket, prover threads, parallel apply and overlay, the default cursor mode, the ready-queue heap, signature batch sizes, the stateless cache and workers); every execution limit of [pipeline] lost its key and alias (cfg.pipeline.node_schema). GOV_DEBUG_TRACE_PIPELINE and GOV_ALIAS_FRONTIER_TELEMETRY switch tracing and telemetry; neither is a field of the execution-policy digest. Fraud service transport remains local file configuration and no longer has environment aliases.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of the inputs that say which chain a node joins: CHAIN, CHAIN_DISCRIMINANT, GENESIS_EXPECTED_HASH, GENESIS_EXPECTED_HASH_FILE, GENESIS_MANIFEST_JSON and GENESIS_PUBLIC_KEY.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: an operator names the chain and pins its genesis.
entries.note: They select and authenticate the genesis a node starts from. A node with another value follows another chain or refuses to start; within one chain every rule comes from that signed genesis and the State committed after it. They are not a production-versus-integration condition: no code compares them with a network name.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of retained node-configured validity or peer-availability conditions: the governance policy (GOV_* voting, bond, slashing, council and viral incentive fields), the peer OpenSSL preview equality flag (CRYPTO_SM_OPENSSL_PREVIEW), the Nexus fee asset and sink (NEXUS_FEE_*), the oracle history depth, the fee account PIPELINE_GAS_TECH_ACCOUNT_ID and COMPUTE_ENABLED.
entries.decided_by: Committed State decides the remaining semantic policy fields (cfg.governance, cfg.oracle, cfg.nexus.policy, cfg.pipeline.gas_identity); a committed field keeps no node-local alias. Optional local OpenSSL acceleration preview must not choose peer eligibility: its equality requirement remains an open availability gate, independently of the fixed IVM relation and the authenticated handshake.
entries.note: Read alias by alias against the fields of the execution-policy digest and the Nexus policy preimage. COMPUTE_ENABLED is listed here because its field enables the compute lane; the digest does not bind it and its owner decides whether it is a service switch. Fraud semantic keys and their environment aliases were retired with the committed policy owner (cfg.fraud.committed_policy); this does not close the remaining local policy families. Crypto admission allowlist aliases were retired with the committed owner; only default hash, SM2 generation DistID and intrinsic dispatch are separately classified in env.crypto.local_preferences. CRYPTO_SM_OPENSSL_PREVIEW remains here: irohad advertises it in CryptoHandshakeCaps and peer.rs can return HandshakeCryptoMismatch when preview matching is required.
entries.open_reason: The remaining semantic node-policy fields require their own committed owners and generators. Independently, irohad still copies crypto.enable_sm_openssl_preview into CryptoHandshakeCaps, and peer handshake validation can reject a differing or absent remote preview flag when require_sm_openssl_preview_match is set. Local SM verification equivalence does not remove this peer-availability condition.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of local service settings: Torii, P2P, Connect, logging, telemetry, snapshots, tiered storage, concurrency, NTS, ISO bridge, Norito codec, keys and addresses.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: transport, storage, observability and identity of this process.
entries.note: Attributed by prefix. A validity-affecting field added under one of these prefixes would need its own entry.

entries.gates: `confidential.enabled`, `confidential.assume_valid` and `confidential.verifier_backend` of the node configuration: a validator refuses to start without confidential verification, an observer may accept confidential blocks without verifying them, and the three values are advertised and compared in the P2P handshake (ConfidentialHandshakeCaps; a mismatch is HandshakeConfidentialMismatch).
entries.decided_by: Delete (plan-author decision of this task): verification implementations ship unconditionally and supported proofs are always verified; an observer that does not verify is not a mode of this release. The handshake keeps the release-bound confidential feature digest only (the rules version and the protocol-default policy hash; it reads no State since this change).
entries.open_reason: Deleting them changes the P2P handshake record, its comparison and its tests in iroha_p2p, the validator start checks of irohad and the localnet, test-network, profile and Taira configurations that write the keys. The handshake record is pinned field by field as protocol carrier `peer_handshake` in crates/iroha_core/src/state/state_table_inventory_tests.rs and specs/state_table_inventory.json (`ConfidentialHandshakeCaps.assume_valid`, `.verifier_backend`, `HandshakeConfidentialMeta.assume_valid`, `.verifier_backend`), files of G.1/BH.3 that are being edited in this wave and that F.4 may not change; the deletion is filed as a shared-file request for the integration pass. It is not a validity change of a validator (which must already run with enabled=true, assume_valid=false). TODO(F.4) at the handshake caps in irohad and at the schema fields in iroha_config.

entries.gates: Reads and writes of `config.zk` outside the configuration crate: the daemon installing local resources into State (install_node_zk), starting the local diagnostic ZK lane from the node's own verifier settings, FASTPQ prover selection, device labels and the compatibility probe; the staged-genesis builder and the test network installing the same local resources; and the localnet builder passing the settings value to the execution-policy digest.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: the settings value a configuration produces holds this node's local resources and the protocol-default validity values, because the node schema has no validity field (cfg.zk.node_schema).
entries.note: Negative test: installs_actual_zk_and_settlement_config_before_kura_replay (irohad) asserts that an SCCP limit placed in a settings value by hand does not reach State. The writes are `config.zk.fastpq.*` assignments of the daemon's FASTPQ command-line overrides. The two startup_preparation reads moved from main: one configures local FASTPQ sidecar limits, and one supplies node ZK resources to snapshot recovery before the same install/replay boundary; neither introduces an independent validity-policy owner. iroha_test_network retained_genesis.rs passes the runtime ZK configuration to config::validate_genesis_with_runtime_config, which installs it through install_node_zk (local resources only); the committed policy of the genesis under validation supplies validity.

entries.gates: `pipa_r.enabled` and `stark.enabled`: retained Core proof verification, verifying-key registration and host ZK syscalls reject a disabled backend, and the Torii prover worker skips it. The standalone IVM host and mock no longer carry these backend switches; their envelope-only behavior does not establish production proof verification.
entries.decided_by: Delete (plan-author decision of this task): both verifiers are always on. Until then the switches are fields of the committed policy (cfg.zk.validity_policy) with the protocol default `true`, so two validators cannot differ and no node configuration can turn one off.
entries.open_reason: Deleting the two fields changes the preimage of compute_zk_consensus_policy_hash, that is the confidential feature digest of every block header, and the ZK term of the execution-policy digest signed into genesis. It is an incompatible change of the `genesis` and `execution_semantics` surfaces: the pinned first-release history is regenerated and the cutover declared in the same change (specs/first_release_history_cutover.json, owned by BH.2 in this wave), and the authority-registry projection (state/authority_registry/zk_policy.rs, G.1) and the `zk-stark` feature gate (feature.zk_stark) change with it. Not done in this change; TODO(F.4) at the two fields in iroha_data_model::zk_validity_policy.

entries.gates: Any writer of the State-owned ZK or pipeline settings other than the installers: a mutable borrow, `mem::replace`, `mem::swap`, `clone_from` or an assignment from another module or crate.
entries.decided_by: The fields `State::zk` and `State::pipeline` are private. Code outside the State modules reads local resources through `State::installed_zk` and `State::installed_pipeline` and validity values through `zk_snapshot`, `pipeline_snapshot`, a view or a block; it cannot name the fields, so the installers (`install_node_zk`, `install_node_pipeline`) are the only production writers by construction. Test builds add `edit_zk_for_testing` and `edit_pipeline_for_testing`, which install the edited value through `set_zk` and `set_pipeline`. The one mutable borrow the scan finds, `block_zk: &mut fields.zk` in state.rs, hands the frozen settings copy of a block to its transaction; it is a field of `StateBlock`, not the State-owned value. Making the fields private exposed one reader of the installed value where the committed policy was meant: Torii's proof-retention status now reads `zk_snapshot()`.

entries.gates: A protocol-default verification gas schedule or default settings value used where the schedule or limits frozen in a block or view must be used.
entries.decided_by: Every production site is listed and the scan fails on a new one. gas.rs defines `DEFAULT_ZK_GAS`, the protocol default as a constant for tests, benches and the State-free overlay builder. The three `CoreHost` constructors in smartcontracts/ivm/host.rs start with it and `set_zk_config` replaces it with the block's frozen schedule for every State-backed host. `staged_default_pipeline` in crates/iroha_deploy builds the pipeline settings of genesis staging, and the genesis block runs under the protocol default. No meter, admission or fee-quote call passes the constant: queue admission and the fee bound are tested under a committed schedule that differs from it, on a node that installed a third one.

entries.gates: Every assignment to the State-owned pipeline settings value or to a field below it.
entries.decided_by: Installed State settings assignments do not author execution limits. The scanner also sees the two StateParameters.pipeline assignments, which cache a validated committed limit policy or its protocol default in the same original parameter MV value; they do not install node policy. The whole State settings value is stored by the private `install_pipeline_settings`, reached in production only through `State::install_node_pipeline`, which strips validity values first (`node_local_resources`). The test-fixture constructor (`configure_test_runtime_defaults`) writes four local scheduling settings (`parallel_apply`, `parallel_overlay`, `ready_queue_heap`, `workers`). The executor no longer refreshes pipeline gas from transaction-local writes; fee settlement restores the predecessor-frozen copy captured at admission. The committed fee projection and remaining integration verification are cfg.pipeline.gas_identity. `State::set_pipeline` exists in test builds only, and the scan reports any new install or write (detectors pipeline_settings_install, pipeline_settings_write).

entries.gates: Confidential verification gas was metered from one process-wide schedule (ZK_GAS_BASE_VERIFY and four more) rather than from the ZK settings a block froze.
entries.decided_by: The schedule is an argument of the meter: `meter_instruction`, `meter_instructions`, `confidential_gas_cost` and `sum_confidential_gas_costs` take the verification gas schedule of the executing block (`StateBlock::zk.gas`, the committed `zk_validity_policy_v1` or the protocol default). The executor and trigger execution pass the transaction's frozen settings, the IVM host the settings it was configured with for the block, queue admission and the fee quotes the schedule of the view they read. The five process statics, their installers and the test lock are deleted; two States with different committed schedules run in one process. Torii's configuration record, the telemetry gauges and `iroha confidential gas get` report the schedule State charges. The four meters now return the original VerificationRefusal if native proof metadata cannot be read, before producing a price; this local failure is not a zero-cost quote or a change of schedule.

entries.gates: Torii's private-settlement route controller is created from an environment variable naming a control directory (Controller::from_env); the module belongs to the `test-network-private-settlement-route-control` feature surface.
entries.decided_by: Remove from production builds, or keep strictly as a test-network fault-injection hook that cannot be compiled into a validator release.

entries.gates: Torii's attachment sanitizer child process recognizes its role and its input bound from three environment variables set by the parent Torii process.

entries.gates: Build-time environment values (git commit, Cargo features, target triple) compiled into the release identity a node reports.
entries.decided_by: Stays evidence metadata.

entries.gates: Developer environment flags that disable or force-fail the Metal and CUDA self-tests (IVM_DISABLE_METAL, IVM_FORCE_METAL_SELFTEST_FAIL, IVM_DEBUG_METAL_SELFTEST, CUDA trace).

entries.decided_by: Remove. No all-protocol qualification record; each implemented protocol is valid independently by its own committed relation and keys.

entries.decided_by: Per-proof relation, parameter and resource validity of the completed maximum transport (X.2 to X.4); no readiness certificate.

entries.gates: The local ZK lane drops a queued diagnostic task after a wall-clock enqueue wait (ingress_enqueue_timeout, dispatch_enqueue_timeout).
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: the lane checks IVM diagnostic traces in the background for telemetry.

These deadlines are committed coordinates: generation/read projections retain immutable trust deadlines. registration::retained_pin binds until_ms to the exact retained generation and checks the canonical block timestamp plus committed committee_heartbeat_ms and the fixed protocol PIN_MARGIN_MS against every retained successor. The moved native message projection and its separate local request deadlines are distinguished in sccp.native_read_controls. No Instant-based request timeout is classified as a committed route deadline here. smartcontracts/isi/sccp/reference_fixture_support.rs holds test-only fixture DATA (its own header says so): it is reached only through `#[path]` declarations inside the `#[cfg(test)] mod reference_fixtures;` modules of forgery.rs, governance/registration.rs and liability/tests.rs, which the scan cannot follow because the inner declarations carry no cfg(test) of their own. entries.gates: Local admitted native proof reads and committed-view forgery prechecks use the original request deadline and cancellation token.
entries.decided_by: Local expiry stops the read/precheck. Synchronous execution reauthenticates the original parent with VerificationControl::Synchronous and committed liability time; a precheck grants no execution authority.
entries.note: Instant::now comparisons in read/native.rs and forgery.rs produce Deadline or Cancelled, not an invalid-evidence verdict. The HTTP owner preserves its incoming RouteExecutionDeadline; it does not reset a clock per stage. The execution.rs Deadline occurrence is a defensive local-refusal match which arms StateStorageAdmissionError and cannot publish an R-EX rejection; synchronous verification carries no local timer. The scanner aggregates all deadline identifiers per file, so the read/native.rs row also includes deadline_ms copied from and compared against the committed message record: that field binds original payload terms and is not a wall-clock expiration check. These are distinct from the committed registration/generation deadlines in sccp.time_budget. No new runtime qualification is claimed by this source census. Coalition, evidence, fast-pause and metadata reads and the forgery keeper retain the same original request deadline. Their committed message/deployment deadline projections do not introduce a second local validity clock.

Missing or inconsistent original source/rotation custody remains unavailable, not authenticated absence; actual Pruned has its own response. UnsupportedScope requires the actual Global root. Request deadline/cancellation is 408 and local capacity or source refusal is 503, with no-store responses. Forgery synchronous execution rechecks the original parent and uses a sticky local storage refusal for missing/inconsistent source or resource failure before any deterministic result can publish; bad signed evidence remains a separate protocol rejection. Native evidence-record and funded-attribution decoders explicitly refuse SCCP data: they are not the independent SccpRestore archive reauthentication owner selected by sumeragi/evidence/restoration.rs. Light-client profile absence still arms VerifierArtifactsUnavailable during execution, and fee-sink absence remains a deterministic pending reason. RegisterRoute launch gaps remain sccp.qualification. The block hook now calls generation/anchor pruning, which preserves pending forgery penalties and retained generation boundaries. The CLI TON evidence helper (iroha_cli sccp/ton.rs) turns BuildError::Unavailable of the account-state proof builder into no evidence (`Ok(None)`): a local client outcome, not authenticated absence. Current forgery/read proofs preserve UnsupportedGeometry and the original physical pairing/allocation refusal; neither is authenticated absence. entries.gates: An untrusted engineering fingerprint locates a possible native proving-key artifact.
entries.decided_by: The strict original artifact import reconstructs the circuit tables, descriptor binding and verifying-key selector commitments.
entries.note: The source fingerprint is only a lookup hint and excludes cryptographic authority. keys/keygen.rs and keys/pk/artifact.rs require from_artifact_v2_cancellable to compare actual source tables and bindings before accepting a key; digest equality cannot authorize a proof or bypass the relation. The `source_digest` of a source-bound key is the fingerprint of reconstructed tables: keygen.rs compares a freshly computed fingerprint with it, and keygen/rebuild.rs recomputes it from the actual circuit before proving and refuses a mismatch with the seal, including for an original admitted through the compiled built-in profile (entry plonk.builtin_source_profile).

entries.gates: Closed compiled source-profile admission of a PLONK verifying-key original (BuiltinSourceProfileV1::match_actual, BuiltinSourceMemberV1::admit_originals_*): a profile is admitted only when its exact bytes match an entry of the table generated into this binary (keys/keygen/builtin/generated.rs) and the build-computed source identity, the complete source closure and the supported compile target agree; otherwise UnsupportedProfile, StaleSource, UnsupportedTarget or IncompleteSourceClosure.
entries.decided_by: Outside the ZK delivery plan: the only production callers are KAGEMUSHA wallet owners, which select it explicitly instead of strict source reconstruction (plonk.source_lookup).
entries.note: BuiltinSourceProfileV1, BuiltinSourceMemberV1 and builtin_source_identity_v1 are called in production only by the KAGEMUSHA producer inventory (iroha_core_zk kagemusha_wallet_artifacts_v1: wallet.rs qualify_wallet_builtin, builtin.rs, operation.rs, sigma.rs), the KAGEMUSHA proof crate (iroha_kagemusha_proof OriginalAdmission::Builtin), the wallet bridge (connect_norito_bridge kagemusha_wallet_ffi/installed.rs) and the offline kagemusha_wallet_artifacts tool; no validator path and no product of the ZK delivery plan calls it. Availability there depends on the binary: the generated table, the build-computed source digest and the compile target. This is a binary/source-digest gate in the sense of F.4; it is recorded here, out of plan with the rest of KAGEMUSHA, and becomes open F.4 work as soon as any operation of the delivery plan admits an original through it. Later proving still rebuilds the actual source and compares its digest (plonk.source_lookup).

entries.decided_by: The original independent finality verifier authenticates supplied proof bytes; local source or allocation refusal cannot supply a proof verdict.
entries.note: VerificationError retains the original FinalityReadError through the terminal N-API projection and reports GenericFailure rather than InvalidArg. This records the finality-read path only; the separately documented block-wire decoder terminal ABI remains incomplete.

entries.gates: A finite local autonomous FASTPQ attempt uses one absolute deadline across finality acquisition, source recovery, isolated canonical replay, proving and durable publication.
entries.decided_by: Expiry retains the exact selected source and incomplete owners for a subsequent existing-worker tick; synchronous proof work is checked after completion and its result retained. It cannot produce a payment rejection, change execution effects or establish settlement.
entries.note: The deadline bounds a local scheduling turn, not eventual completion. max_native_steps bounds each cooperative replay continuation. Genuine H1/H2 proof publication and process/network liveness still require their separate acceptance tests; the clock names alone do not establish those outcomes. The current producer passes the same absolute deadline through split select/read/replay/advance/persist phases; retries retain the exact selected source and prior incomplete owners.

entries.gates: Environment aliases for local hash/SM2 generation preferences and SM acceleration dispatch.
entries.decided_by: Committed CryptoAdmissionPolicyV1 decides ordinary algorithm admission; IVM omitted SM2 DistID uses Sm2PublicKey::DEFAULT_DISTID. Local preferences select generation or acceleration, not a carried transaction verdict.
entries.note: Crypto::parse retains these three local controls: default_hash, sm2_distid_default and sm_intrinsics. OpenSSL preview is excluded here because CryptoHandshakeCaps plus required preview equality can reject a peer; that alias remains open F.4 in env.config.validity_family_aliases. An unsupported forced acceleration choice is a node-start configuration failure, not a validator-selectable consensus rule. sm_syscalls_ignore_local_crypto_preferences exercises fixed results across local preferences. This classification does not close general feature-dependent verifier availability (feature.sm_gost_bls_pqc).

entries.gates: The anonymous-ballot transaction entrypoint has no completed authenticated State/context verifier and execution adapter. Admission, routing, queue, block and certified lane merge refuse that entrypoint before ordinary authority/route selection.
entries.decided_by: P.8 must supply the real authenticated context and ballot execution relation. Until then the unconditional accurate typed refusal must remain; deleting it cannot make the operation valid.
entries.note: tx.rs explicitly TODO(E2) marks the missing adapter. AnonymousBallotUnavailable becomes ExecutionDeferred::VerifierInitializationUnavailable and never a committed rejection, but this transport does not make the missing implementation an incidental local resource. Torii projects the same unfinished boundary. Its lib.rs row includes two AnonymousBallotUnavailable identifiers and two bootle_lantern_issuance_unavailable_response_v1 service helpers; only the former are the unfinished ballot adapter. No completion or release readiness is claimed. The ten tx.rs hits are five AnonymousBallotUnavailable and five anonymous_ballot_unavailable identifiers. Generic CryptoImplementationUnavailable in the same non-family file is outside this detector row, not assigned to P.8; its provenance is open M.2 in crypto.implementation_unavailable.

entries.gates: A known canonical algorithm lacks its required implementation in this build on PGC signature or SCCP recipient admission. This is compiled-feature dependence, not allocator, device or entropy refusal.
